executive_assessment.text: Evidence distinguishes Sava floodplain exposure, projected Sava-tributary flows and named municipal exposure, vulnerability and coping-capacity patterns; composite indices are not event forecasts.

The 2014 recovery assessment documents flooding/landslides moving legacy mines and recovery work requiring survey and clearance. This is a conflict-legacy interaction, not climate causing the original conflict.
The 2024 rapid assessment identifies remote-area access/service gaps and anticipated protection risks. These and selected municipal capacities have explicit assessment and outcome limits.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2021-09 reports: The NAP reports 1961–2018 warming (annual 0.4–1.2°C; growing-season up to 1.4°C), rising heavy-rainfall share and variability; it names Trebinje, Zenica, Laktaši and Sanski Most among repeatedly affected towns.

Source dated 2021-09 reports: Record May 2014 rain plus snowmelt broke Sava embankments and flooded Central Posavina, Odžačka Posavina and Semberija; later heavy rain caused repeat flooding and landslides.
Source dated 2014-06-30 reports: After the May 2014 floods, 81 municipalities suffered impacts; about 90,000 people were displaced and more than 40,000 sheltered or stayed with relatives.

Source dated 2014-06-30 reports: Floods and landslides shifted mines/UXO from marked or suspected areas; 51 of 3,000 reported landslides were in suspected hazardous areas, and 105 km² was flagged as potentially contaminated.

Source dated 2014-06-30 reports: Residents in Posavina and Brčko reported mines/UXO near homes; repair and reconstruction in unsafe areas were restricted pending survey and clearance, leaving farmers and workers at risk.

Source dated 2022-11 reports: Bihać, Bijeljina and Gradačac established local DRR platforms, adopted aligned strategies and risk assessments, and reported engineering measures and shock-responsive social-protection plans.

Source dated 2022-11 reports: Busovača's scorecard names floods as its main hazard; it reports no training for poorest groups, recent business continuity plans in only 20–40% of firms, and warning reach of about half the population.
Source dated 2022-11 reports: Jajce reports an outdated risk assessment, no training for poorest groups, continuity plans in under 20% of firms and warning reach below half the population.

Source dated 2026-06 reports: INFORM ranks Brod (7.5) and Bihać (7.3) highest for exposure; Neretva municipalities Konjic and Mostar face flood/landslide risks, and about 12,000 people in Konjic live in landslide-prone areas.
Source dated 2026-06 reports: The report records a 2024 Jablanica landslide that buried buildings and killed 19 people, although its municipal hazard-exposure score was moderate.

Source dated 2026-06 reports: Trnovo (RS) and Foča score 7.4 for vulnerability with unemployment above 20%; the report links job scarcity partly to war-damaged economies and says benefit dependence hampers post-disaster recovery.

Source dated 2026-06 reports: Bosansko Grahovo, Livno and Kupres score poorly on coping capacity; Bosansko Grahovo's road density is under one-seventh the national average, constraining evacuation and aid access.

Source dated 2024-11-21 reports: The rapid assessment says road and bridge damage restricted movement from remote areas and slowed recovery; in Jablanica it counted 483 affected people and 188 evacuees across interviewed flood-hit locations.

Source dated 2024-11-21 reports: The assessment calls for mobile maternal, reproductive and psychological care for women and girls in remote areas; it names social-care staffing shortages in Jablanica, Konjic and Kiseljak.

known_gaps.text: No inspected primary source establishes current armed or intercommunal violence disrupting adaptation or disaster-risk-reduction delivery. The clearest conflict interaction is legacy mine/UXO contamination affecting flood recovery; INFORM also documents war-related economic scarring and weaker disaster recovery.
The 2021 NAP is a dated institutional baseline; later legal and spatial-planning reforms were not verified. Its Sava flood model does not cover the Adriatic watershed.
The 2026 INFORM index excludes disaster-risk-reduction capability and humanitarian coping indicators because of insufficient data; its composite rankings are not event warnings.

The UNDRR municipal scorecards are selected local self-assessments from 2021–2022, and the 2024 MIRA is a purposive key-informant snapshot rather than a representative or independently verified post-disaster assessment.
The MIRA GBV statement is a conditional risk attributed to a separate UN Women rapid gender report; this collection did not independently inspect that separate report.
Jablanica is retained without the intake's erroneous Central Bosnia Canton tag.
Historical mine-recovery restrictions and 2024 anticipated GBV risks are not current incident or service-status reports.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
